replication.target_description: Effect of Financial Communication on Relationship Satisfaction Published2024 article pp.2536–2538, cross-sectional actor and partner effects, plus longitudinal effects pp.2538–2539. Locator does not distinguish spouse, actor/partner path or model.

n.sample_role: Newlywed mixed-gender dyads; final overall analytical sample is1,079, but no unique target test assigned.
n.exclusions: Overall study retains continuous marriages W1–W5 and excludes34 same-gender couples; specific target test remains ambiguous.

es.location: p.2537 Direct effects and Figure1; pp.2538–2539 longitudinal results

notes: Duplicate neutral descriptions52/53 and54/55 provide no mapping to husbands versus wives or actor versus partner paths. No row-order inference made. Satisfaction has four distinct cross-sectional paths (own and partner for each spouse), and financial disagreements likewise has four paths. Rendered PDF p.2537 visually checked. Canonical TXT omits negative signs from financial-disagreement beta coefficients that are visible in PDF narrative and Figure1; parent transcription check required before any signed coefficient extraction. Generic discussion verdict is about mediation hypotheses, not a uniquely identified target path, so reported_success remains null.
